corpus.notes: Read all 72 open issues (titles+labels) and fetched bodies/comments for plausible matches (#26, #38). Corpus is exceptionally well-covered for perf: nearly every hot-path allocation/cache/blocking-IO issue already filed (#170-#227 span layout, cascade, net, storage, paint, text). Roadmap epic #40-#48 left alone. Weighted attention to churn since 2026-07-01 (v0.0.14-v0.0.19): rendering parity, hinted glyph raster + glyph cache, CSS light-dark()/var() IACVT, :is/:where/:has, grid explicit numeric line placement, min/max/clamp, table-nesting cap, negative z-index, Windows scroll perf. Both plausible enrichment targets (#26 SiblingRef :has children clone; #38 glyph cache in v0.0.16) already carried thorough, up-to-date follow-up comments from prior runs — left quiet to honor the no-duplicate-noise gate.

findings.title: Grid explicit numeric line placement allocates an unbounded occupancy grid — grid-row: 2000000000 in page CSS exhausts memory and aborts the browser
Nested repeat() in grid-template track parsing multiplies the per-level 1000 cap — repeat(1000, repeat(1000, 1px)) expands to 1M+ tracks at parse time

enrichments_considered_but_skipped.reason: The :has() SiblingRef child-clone broadening is already captured verbatim in the 2026-07-18 follow-up comment (fp-update sibling-ref-has-children-clone) — no new detail to add.

The v0.0.16 glyph-cache implementation (incl. the remaining unhinted-fallback re-outline and the unbounded HintingInstance cache spun off as #205) is already documented in the 2026-08-02 follow-up comment (fp-update glyph-cache-implemented-v0016).

duplicates_skipped: grid-row DoS vs #170 nested-flex/grid-exponential (distinct: #170 is 2^depth re-measurement of subtrees; #226 is a single item's huge line number sizing the occupancy grid)
grid-row/repeat DoS vs #201/#220 table-nesting and #177 calc-recursion (same DoS class, different subsystem/root cause)

JSON recursive-descent parser depth (json.rs) — wire format is flat (nodes[] with flat children id lists), so parse depth is bounded ~4; not attacker-deep; DOM tree walkers already bounded by MAX_OPEN_DEPTH=512 per #224
no_findings_areas: cerberus-net decompress.rs: MAX_DECOMPRESSED=64MB bomb guard enforced during inflation — sound
grid column sizing: auto-fill capped at 64, repeat() capped 1000/level (only the ROW placement and NESTED repeat escape the caps — filed as #226/#227)
cerberus-js-dom wire format: flat node map, bounded JSON parse depth; U+2028/2029 eval-splice escaping in place
cerberus-crypto/tls/dns bombs and net header/body caps: already covered by prior filings (#186/#180/#210/#221)
overall_health: Very good and well-audited. The perf/efficiency surface is thoroughly covered by ~50 prior open issues; this rotated deep-dive found the codebase in strong shape and surfaced two genuinely new untrusted-input allocation DoS bugs, both introduced by the post-2026-07-01 CSS grid work: an unbounded grid-row occupancy allocation (high) and a nested-repeat() track-expansion amplification (medium). No new stale-but-fixed issues; the two obvious enrichment targets already carry current follow-up comments, so nothing was re-commented.
